utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Good morning, Mr. Gasi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning. [Interpretation] Good morning, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor, have you come back with the analysis of your associate exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I have indeed, Mr. President. I'll just read the associated exhibits into the transcript if I may. We'll be tendering 65 ter numbers 08174, 07669, 07466, 08405, 06940, the next one has already been admitted as P102.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. 7466 and what is the number after 7466?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Then 6940. The next has been admitted as P102. The next is 7485. 7345. 11439.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, but I think that's a duplicate or copy of 11441, and I think that 11441 is of better quality.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. President. We'll tender 11441.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The next is 06959.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That ends the associated exhibits, and we've uploaded as P3002 the transcript of the evidence of this witness redacted in accordance with Your Honours' decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic. Please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellency. Good morning Excellency. Good morning everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Gasi.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We left off yesterday when I asked you for how long you were a member of the SDA and the Executive Committee and I was a bit perplexed with regard to that. You said that you were in that position only for a few months before the election, but in some states -- statements you say that you were a member between the 26th of May 1990 and November 1992?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible, but let us -- let me make it clear for you. I can tell you that I intimately still feel a member of the SDS -- SDA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do not overlap, please. Put a pause. Mr. Gasi, just wait before you start answering, please. Yes, Mr. Karadzic. Repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you in some negative context. I'm just curious to know in what capacity you participated in the political life of Brcko after the elections. Did you participate in the political life in Brcko after the elections?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. Once I resigned as a member of the Executive Committee, I never attended a single meeting of the SDA party in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. But if you were a member until November 1991, that means to say that during that period prior to multi-party elections for a year you took part in the political life.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but only up until the elections. Otherwise, I did not take part in it afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In what capacity did you attend Municipal Assembly meetings?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simply as an observer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we quickly look at 1D3893 in e-court. Let's look at page 6. Here you confirm that you attended meetings of the Municipal Assembly. Can you see that if we can locate it. Lines 1 and 2. [In English] "What were your duties in that capacity?" "Well, I attended meetings. I did not have any special duties." "Do you recall the elections that were held in your area ...," and so on and so on.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I attended rallies before the elections, but I did not hold any position or any office.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection to the question made by the accused. He said -- he's putting to the witness an inconsistency which is not, in fact, in the transcript. The previous page of this transcript states that the witness's answer is: "A member of the town's Executive Committee of the town of Brcko." And then the question comes: "What were your duties in that capacity?" So in my submission Mr. Karadzic is deliberately mixing up the Executive Committee of the town of Brcko and the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, the witness confirmed, but I probably didn't give you the proper reference page, but the witness confirmed and I know from other sources that he attended Municipal Assembly meeting during the multi-party period. That is what he confirmed today as well and he did that as an observer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe I attended two such meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So were you familiar with the policies pursued by the SDA and the activists who were in the SDA in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were among the top seven people in the SDA at the time.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the SDA have a Crisis Staff in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your testimony in the Tadic case, you said that in Muslim villages there were no weapons; correct?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's look at a letter that you wrote to the "Ljiljan" magazine. Will you please tell the Chamber something about this periodical?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I did not write that letter, and I know nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's not your letter?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How do you know which letter I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've been asked before in this court about this letter, and I'm telling you now that I'm not capable of writing such a kind of letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now have a look at 1D3888, and we'll see that perhaps after all it was you who wrote that letter?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can look at it as much as you want, but I'm telling you I'm not the author of that letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you in this country that was blackened out here - I think it's Denmark - at the time?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was in Denmark.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The first sentence says that you are addressing the readership of the "Ljiljan" magazine, that you had listened to BH radio and then you are giving a comprehensive assessment. Can we have the last page, please. "Your loyal reader, Isak Gasi." Is this your address?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, it seems that this is, after all, a letter that you wrote.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The man who wrote this letter now lives in America. He used to be a journalist before the war in Brcko. I did not write this letter, although this is my address.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you did read it, and you signed it, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not sign it in the sense to confirm that I authored it. I signed it as a reader who was interviewed by this journalist, but this is not my letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ah-ha. So only the answers that you gave are yours?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now have page 1. Somewhere in line ten from the top, it says that the preparation for the occupation of Brcko by the JNA started several months before the war officially started. "We, the naive Bosniaks, were led astray by our leadership." Do you think that the JNA was illegally in Brcko in 1991?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't illegally in Brcko in 1991. Moreover, it was not an illegal force even until May of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By the way, if this letter or interview, this article, is discussed in previous proceedings, why do we not have a translation?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We sent it to be translated. We still haven't got it back, and I don't know whether it was translated for the previous trials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have page 2 of this letter, or apparently this was done in the form of an interview, but it was printed in the form of a letter; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You might be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's look at first two lines. "When we saw that the devil came, we started to arm ourselves covertly. We paid 800 German marks for a single rifle."

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see this language that concerns the arming is nothing that I uttered. I did not discuss it with this gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that it was his language and his formulation?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I never said anything to this effect. I never spoke about arming.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the Tadic case, on page 705 and 706, you testified that people in the Serbian villages wore military uniforms but that there were no such people in Muslim villages.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us today that in April of 1992 there were no armed Muslims in Muslim villages?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know and as far as I was able to see, I saw none of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now have 1D3893, which is your testimony in the Tadic case. Here you say that those were reserve uniforms of the JNA. Does that mean that these men were registered with the JNA, but according to the law, were the people in Muslim and Croat villages also reservists of the JNA? Sorry, this is page 9 and 10. Nine and then 10. The last two lines. The question was: "After that mobilisation call do you remember seeing any men in Serb villages wearing military uniforms?" Can we have page 10. And you see that up to line 5 you said - you can read English - that you didn't see such things in Muslim villages. Were all able-bodied men in all villages, Serbian, Muslim, and Croat, according to the law in force at the time reservists of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Right. But you allege that the people from the Muslim villages did not respond to the call-up, they had no uniforms or weapons?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if the people from Muslim or Croat villages responded to the call-up, but I personally did not see people in Croat or Muslim villages dressed in uniforms or carrying weapons. I am 100 per cent sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now again have 1D3888. You say at the time Bosniaks and Croats left active duty service in the JNA. The gaps were, as a rule, filled by Serbs. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. We don't have to call up this document then?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I would like to object again to the form of the question. In the question you said, You say that, and the witness has already given evidence that that earlier document, 1D3888, is not his letter but simply something created by a journalist which contains parts of what Mr. Gasi said. So I object to the form of the question made by the accused there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we can understand and we can proceed, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm not going to insist on this unless the witness confirms that parts of this is true. This is actually his knowledge about the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now have a look at 1D3876.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are you tendering that letter?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. For identification pending translation, and as I said, we already sent it to the CLSS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1563, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is a report regarding paramilitary organisations that was compiled by the command of the 17th Corps, that is to say before the war in 1991?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems that the command of the 17th Corps had written up this report. I have no reason not to believe that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have page 7 of this document. Do you agree that the JNA is describing the paramilitary organisation of all three parties here, and it says paramilitary formations of the HDZ, and it says here that they did not form their own paramilitary organisations here, but they did work on arming their members. And they were not organised into military units. At the same time, the HDZ has recruited its members into the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia, and then villages are being listed here of these smaller military units, in Ulice, Krepsic, Donja Skakava, Gornja Skakava, Zovik, Bosanska Bijela, Gornji Vuksic, Dubrava, and so on and so forth. Are all of these villages Croatian?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could we please have a clear screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is the majority population there to this day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Could you wait until we have a clear screen. E-court has experienced some difficulty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's better to have a break. We'll a break for ten minutes to solve these technical issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have 1D3876 again, please, and then page 7.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have LiveNote again in e-court. Yes. Now it's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Page 7, that's what we had. It's the army, the JNA, describing the situation in Brcko. We have already spoken about the HDZ, and let us see what it says about the SDA paramilitary formations, the village of Brezevo Polje, a detachment of Muslim believers, diagram number 2 that we are going to look at, then the weapons, what they had. Do you see that part, number 1? And then number 2, paragraph 2, says that they have reliable information to the effect that the SDA had armed most of their extremist members already in the month of October with about 300 pistols and then rifles. And then paragraph 3 says: "As this question was centralised the leadership of the SDA of Brcko is planning to send an SDA brigade at battalion level consisting of the Muslim population living in the territories of the municipalities of Brcko, Gradacac ...," et cetera. And then it also says further on, under C, that a Chetnik detachment of undetermined strength and with an undetermined amount of weapons was formed, following orders of SDS leaders from Brcko and at Seselj's suggestions. Most members of this detachment are volunteers in a JNA unit stationed in the area so that they could undergo training, procure weapons, and ideologically influence the active duty command officers. Obviously, ideologically, they were different from the command of the JNA, right? So the general is suspicious and believes that they will influence his officers. Did you know that things were developing this way, that weapons were being distributed publicly in mosques and in party offices and so on?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I don't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we look at page 22. You were off until the 27th of May; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have page 22 in this document. Can we enlarge this? Did you know Meho Muratovic, Osman Kavazovic, Sako Hadzajlic, Ako Hadzajlic, Dzemila Hadzajlic, Nijaz Dzidza? You see these names here. Did you know these men?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know or do you see now that this was a brigade of Muslim believers in Brezevo Polje and that later on it was the basis for a four battalion brigade that already became operational in May in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see this paper. I see this diagram. Whether this actually existed, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your statement you said that true fighting had started. Who was engaged in this fighting? In town itself you said that there was true fighting.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: True fighting? I did not say true fighting. I did see artillery, though. That belonged to the JNA at the time, and it was firing perhaps every 10 or 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that part of your statement. Did you know Farid Mujkanovic?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know who that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that in Brcko there was also a staff and a detachment of the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know Ibrahim Ramic?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know Ibrahim Ramic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was his function?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was president of the SDA of the city board.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mustafa Ramic?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's the brother of Dr. Ibro Ramic, and he was the elected president of the Municipal Assembly of Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. Do you know that in all 103 municipalities except for the Croat municipalities there was a Municipal Staff of the Patriotic League and a brigade?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know about that, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know Rasid Guso?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have you heard of him?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not during the war while I was in Brcko. Later on I read something about him in the newspapers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you were born in that town and you were a well-known man in that town whom. How come you didn't know? Did you know Miralem Jukic, nicknamed Skorpija?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we're going to abandon this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karadzic. All this witness testified about this document is that he would not doubt the authenticity of this document, but he didn't know anything about this document. There's no basis. And this is an example how you are wasting your time. You could have put your case to the witness, and you just could proceed. You read out all the documents that could not be admitted, and that's -- yes. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellency. These were names from another document that I haven't even tendered, a different document. But I just wanted to check what the witness knew out of all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 65 ter 6961. Can we have that now, please. Can we see paragraph 3 down there that has to do with Bijeljina and Brcko. You mentioned that you knew what was going on in Bijeljina. Have a look at paragraph 4. This is the JNA again, the 17th Corps, on the 2nd of April, and in the first part of paragraph 4, it says that the situation did calm down in Brcko -- no, Bijeljina, and it says that the party leaders are not in control and cannot ensure that fighting stops. And then there's a reference to Brcko, the blockade of roads, access to the hospital in Bijeljina, and so on and so forth. And can we now have the next page. Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this something that you knew yourself, that this chaos had reigned?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, in Bijeljina. How far away is Bijeljina from you?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 50 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So it's the neighbouring town, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have the second page -- ah yes, here it is. Brcko, now, you see here it says what the situation is like in Brcko. It says from the morning hours of the 1st of April in front of JNA premises the representatives of parties are moving, calling for a move towards Bijeljina, but others are appealing for peace and order. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know that and I cannot see on my screen what you seem to have read out just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's the second part of paragraph 7, Putnikovo Brdo, so on and so forth and it says, "In Brcko from the morning hours ...." Do you see that, the 1st of April? See where this cursor is now?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see. Mr. Karadzic, I really don't know anything about this. I can not talk about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. 1D3888. Can we have a brief look at that. Did you know that many Muslims had set out towards Bijeljina from various towns and villages, that they wanted to walk on Bijeljina in military fashion?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please look at page 2 of this document. Take a look at this, the second circled paragraph. "At that time, many Bosniaks from Gradacac, Orasje, Srebrenik and surrounding villages came to Brcko to see whether our people in Bijeljina could be assisted. The majority was in favour of moving on Bijeljina, but they were stopped by the leadership from Brcko, the brothers Ibro and Mustafa Ramic." So you say in your interview the same thing that the JNA is saying?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you, Mr. Karadzic, that that interview that I gave to that journalist who wrote this, that has nothing to do with what I had said to him. I don't know anything about this, nothing whatsoever, and I repeat once again, if I knew anything, I'd tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Nevertheless, you put your address and your signature below this interview.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, it is my signature and my address. And how it reached "Ljiljan," I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the previous document? Are you going to admit that, the JNA report of the 2nd of April, 6961?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. We don't have any basis to admit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 1D3881, please. Before the 27th of May, you were able to listen to the radio, watch television, and move freely about the town; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please pay attention to this report by the Radio Bosnia and Herzegovina. They broadcast something that they allegedly received from ham radio operators in Brcko. There is a reference to the artillery opening fire on Brodusa and Dizdarusa, and it says here: "At around 1800 hours, soldiers from the 108 Brcko Brigade started an operation in the area of Bila Gorge. This operation by the special units was successful and they broke through deep into occupied territory destroying in the process one tank, one personnel carrier ...," and so on and so forth. Can you see the date? It was on the 15th of May.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fighting that took place at the time?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was no fighting going on at the time. On the 11th or the 12th of May, I was with Elektrodistribucija, very close to that Kalanac [phoen] gorge. If there had been fighting going on we wouldn't have been able to go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But this is a report dated 19th of May, and Ministry of Defence of the BiH Army stamped that, and this was broadcast on the radio.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can only tell you what I experienced in Brcko from the 1st to the 27th of May, and that doesn't tally with what the document says. The document is here, but I'm not able to comment upon it because the truth of what I saw with my own eyes was different.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is the attitude of the Chamber towards this document? It contradicts the fact that a Crisis Staff existed and that a brigade existed, so what is the attitude of the Trial Chamber towards this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Your Honours, if Your Honours consider this to be of assistance towards the witness's credibility, it would be admissible on that basis. I'd just like to note also that the ABiH stamp on this document bears the date 19th of May, 1992, but I don't think, I'm sure Mr. Karadzic will agree, that the document itself, it's not clear what date it's from. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll admit this document as indicated by Mr. Gaynor for the purpose of the assessment of the credibility of this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1564, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D3877 is the next document I would like to call up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at this. This is a statement by the Brcko municipality Crisis Staff, handwritten and translated, and towards the end, it says, "Soldiers of the 108th Birac Brigade are still holding the line ...," and so on and so forth. There is a description of what is going on. The forces are pulling back towards Bijeljina, and the reporters have observed long columns of refugees and troops in the town. Do you see this statement by the Brcko municipality Crisis Staff press centre? This certainly is not a Serbian Crisis Staff, because it uses derogatory words for Serbs, calling them Chetniks and so on and so forth; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the document that you showed me before this one is where it says in the heading Vares, and this document here in the heading has the words the Public Company Usora Jela. So far as I know this is not in Brcko. This must have arrived from Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gasi, but this is just a block stamp that companies distribute by way of advertising. You can have that anywhere.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I did not see those writing pads in Brcko. This is from Doboj. I don't know who wrote this, where this was written. I can't comment upon this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now look at the last page? Do you see that this was received and stamped by the Ministry of Defence and the BiH Army on the 14th of June, 1992, which means that the Crisis Staff of Brcko municipality, not the Serbian Crisis Staff issued its statement; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is right. You say that this is a stamp and it is a stamp by the Ministry of Defence and the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. However, the paper on which it was written seems to have arrived from Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You were, I would like to object to the authenticity of this document. We're willing to agree that the stamp of the ABiH appears to be authentic. The rest of the document does not appear to bear the usual indicia of reliability and authenticity which are normally present on documents tendered for admission.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be allowed it respond. This is a Prosecutor's document with an ERN number. Obviously they received it either from the Muslim side or from the Ministry of Defence. This statement was probably read out, but before it was read out it was handwritten. It was recorded in writing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Based upon the fact that it was received by the ABiH army, we have a basis to admit this. We'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1565, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know, Mr. Gasi, that people from Brcko, both Muslims and Croats, especially Croats, were leaving and going to Croatia to join the national guards in Croatia, the armed forces of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know such people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that people often crossed the river from Croatia to Brcko, transporting weapons from Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure that I would have seen that, Mr. Karadzic, because I spent a lot of time on the Sava River, and while I was there I didn't see any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you spend nights on the river?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't spend nights on the Sava River.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that those transports of weapons would probably have taken place by night rather than by day?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How far is Orasje from Brcko?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thirty-five kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the blowing up of the bridge in Orasje by the Croatian forces? And that happened before the blowing up of the bridge that you described in your statement, the bridge in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that the bridge in Orasje had been blown up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We have to wait for the interpretation. You should know why I am making pauses. When was the bridge in Orasje blown up?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date, but I think that it was in early April 1992. Perhaps a month before the Brcko bridge was blown up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that that bridge was blown up by Croats?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And under whose control was Orasje throughout the war and before the war?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war? I don't know under whose control it was. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: During the war?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that either, because I did not participate in the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You don't know that Brcko -- or, rather, Orasje was always under HVO control and of the Croatian forces and the vast majority of the population is Croatian?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not a vast majority. There's a vast Muslim majority in Orasje -- rather, was before the war. It wasn't really Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. We'll have a look at the census, and it's going to be easy to see that. Do you know that on the other side of the Sava River there was an improvised bridge before the war broke out in Brcko, in Brcko itself? There was an improvised bridge across the Sava River.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. There were two bridges. Both were damaged, but for someone to have made a third bridge, that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that people could cross the Sava on foot at that time?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, across the old bridge. People went on foot from Croatia to Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the other way round; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that weapons from Croatia were transported from Croatia to Brcko across that bridge as well?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you know that apartments of prominent Serbs in Brcko before the conflict broke out were specially marked?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned that when the conflict broke out people were fleeing, and you mentioned the Serb part of town and the Muslim part of town. Since when has this Serb part of town existed?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I don't understand what you're saying. Fleeing. What do you mean fleeing? From where? Who was fleeing?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that people were seeking shelter, Serbs in the Serb part of town, Muslims in the Muslim part of town.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where did you find that? I didn't say that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the population fleeing from Brcko and within Brcko itself?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. On the 1st and 2nd and 3rd of May, I was moving from my apartment that is close to the garrison of Brcko to Meraje that is, say, half a kilometre away from where I live and that is where my wife's parents live. I did not notice anyone fleeing from town at the time. That is what I saw. I crossed the river and I went back too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us just establish this. You mentioned that there is a Serb part of town in Brcko. Since when?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since -- for as long as I can remember, and I was born in 1957 in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It dates back to the Turkish times; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can I ask for a transcript reference for any further references to Mr. Gasi's prior evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before that, Mr. Karadzic, I'm regularly struggling to understand the relevance of your line of questioning. You have spent almost one and a half hours with this witness, who testified his experience he underwent in the Luka camp, but you didn't ask a single question about it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I think that we spent more time waiting than what I spent, but I think we should take advantage of the opportunity of having a witness who is a sportsman, a popular person in town, a member of the SDA, the top echelons of the SDA at that, and he can shed more light on these developments that led to the creation of Luka and also, by the way, the question of credibility is important, too, but I am going to cut things short. If that is your view, I'm going to cut things short.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Gasi, we are going to move on to Brcko, and after the break I'm going to find a reference in terms of the Serb part of town and the Muslim part of town. You did say there was a Muslim part of town too.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the Serb part of town, I know that very well, and in that Serb part of town there were quite a few Muslims who had their houses and apartments there. Now, why it was called Srpska Varos, the name probably dates back to the old times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But there were Muslim parts of town, predominantly Muslim parts of town; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellencies, I'm asking that because there was a debate in terms of transforming Brcko into three municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of that debate aimed at transforming Brcko into three municipalities so that every municipality would have its own part of the inner city and also the surrounding villages?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This division into three parts, yes, I know about that I heard that at the session of the Municipal Assembly of Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now briefly go back to the question of the destruction of bridges. You said that Rade Bozic informed you that he destroyed the bridge; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you say that the Croatian side destroyed the bridge in Orasje so that the JNA would not cross over from Bosnia to Croatia and that the JNA destroyed the bridge in Brcko so the Croatian Army would not enter Brcko?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I don't know who destroyed the bridge in Orasje. Secondly, I have already told you, and I said many times before this Court that Rade Bozic said to me himself personally that he commanded the operation of destroying the bridges in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that he made a mistake and that he was sorry; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is right. That is what he said. That is literally what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was Rade Bozic a member of the green -- no, Red Berets, some paramilitary group in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, Mr. Rade Bozic was saying that he was a captain of the military police. He did have a red beret.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll go back to that when we have enough time. Let us now take a look at developments in Brcko itself. You say that as soon as the tensions went up in Brcko, you decided to get your family out of Brcko and to take them to Belgrade; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had given such a great deal of thought to tensions in April, Mr. Karadzic, that thanks to a Serb, a good neighbour of mine, I managed to take my wife and daughter with his assistance to Bijeljina on the 30th of April in the afternoon by car. I had no idea of these tensions in town. Had I known, I assure you perhaps I wouldn't be sitting here in this courtroom today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tensions in which town?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why then did you take your wife and daughter out of Brcko?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the wife of that neighbour came to me and said, "Jasminka, it is time for you and your husband and your child to leave Brcko because the war has started." Since I had no connections and no possibility to go either left or right, I went towards Serbia, towards -- to go to Serbia, Belgrade. I went to Serbia. Jovica Bogicevic took me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And after Bijeljina you took them to Belgrade; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bijeljina, I came across this sportsman who is a good friend of mine. He was a member of Yugoslavia's national team, the national team of the former Yugoslavia, and he took Jasminka and Adna [phoen] to Serbia and I went back to Brcko together with Jovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You did not cross over into Serbia then. You came only in June.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When Mr. Rade Bozic took me out, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You do know that by then the war was well underway throughout Bosnia for three weeks, from Sarajevo and further on?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about it. I saw it on TV. Now, whether it was a raging war as you had put it, I cannot say, but there was a war going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, peace had been preserved in Brcko; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that belief I returned. I believed that there would be no problems, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At that time you moved about freely in town while the civilian authorities kept the situation under control in the customary way; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. April, and until the bridges on the Sava River were destroyed; that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I note the time. It's time to take a break if it is convenient.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Excellency. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, Your Honour, I should at the outset introduced a member of my team who is with us today. Rens van der Werf has been a legal assistant on our team for the last six months and he's here for the balance today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Welcome, Mr. van der Werf. Eleven o'clock.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that as part of the efforts to preserve peace in Brcko you had joint patrols -- or, rather, mixed patrols of a mixed ethnic composition; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard that, and I also saw those patrols that existed both in town and outside of town. There were, indeed, mixed patrols composed of civilian police and the military police from the barracks. That's what the city council of Brcko had agreed with the command of the garrison in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You repeated that in the Stanisic case. This is 1D3894, page 18. Can we just have a -- take a brief look, and that contributed to the preservation of peace?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure the number is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was peaceful even before those patrols were set up. Those patrols were introduced because the municipal leadership had negotiated with the military command, and they asked for members of the JNA to be involved in those patrols.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Your answer here starts before the war, and then you continue talking about that.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellencies, I would like to tender all those pages I'm going to call up. I don't know if they will be admitted under one number or several numbers, and if I don't call up the pages I don't wish to tender them, but I would like to tender this particular page that is on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The chief of the police station was a Croat, a member of the HDZ, Stjepan Filipovic, and the commander of that public station was as a Muslim, Zlatko Jasarevic; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Veselic joined only after the break-up of power as part of the judiciary; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what happened in the police station at that time. I don't know when Veselic joined the police station as its chief. I believe that it was on the 2nd or 3rd of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, while the joint police existed, the -- the chief was a Croat from the HDZ, and the commander was a Muslim from the SDA; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then in April the joint authorities still functioned, and Council for National Defence of Brcko organised a meeting and invited appealed for a unit of a mixed composition to be set up; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard of that. You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you say in your interview that you could apply and that the only condition was the person didn't have a criminal record. You say that you volunteered to join that unit and that there was a meeting between the volunteers and the representatives of the municipal authorities who were behind that idea; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we look at 1D3888. I have already tendered the page on the screen. Can this be admitted, and maybe we can preserve the same number, because everything has been already admitted in the Stanisic case?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll see how many pages are going to be tendered and see whether it's wiser to admit it in its entirety. We'll see it later. So this page will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1566, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now look at 1D3888 in e-court, and the translation will probably be on the ELMO. We have it there already. Page 3, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 3.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Page 4 in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say here that among the attendees were representatives of all the three parts of the authorities, Ristanic, Milutinovic, and so on and so forth, and you say that people volunteered en masse and the only condition was that they didn't have criminal records, and then there was a meeting in the culture hall between us volunteers and the municipal representatives. And then you say: "We were surprised to see that the meeting was also attended by Pavle Milinkovic and Milorad Segovac [phoen], representatives of the JNA garrison." And you say: "When we learned whose insignia we were supposed to wear on the uniforms and who we were supposed to be subordinated to, there was commotion and people started leaving the meeting. Mustafa Ramic, a Muslim, and Mustafa Kehunjic [phoen], the secretary of the Secretariat for National Defence of Brcko Municipality, attempted to hold you back and they did everything they could prevent us from leaving the meeting. They tried to rally us once again but this time by issuing call-ups for the reserve, but this attempt failed as well."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Slow down. Slow down, please. What is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question is this: We're talking about a mixed Municipal Council, and they tried to set up a mixed unit of volunteers, and that that attempt would have succeeded if the garrison had not been invited into that unit?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The idea existed, but I wouldn't agree with you when you say that in this letter it says that when Pavle Milinkovic appeared and he was the commander of the garrison, and the other officers, that we dispersed because of that. I personally knew that they would be the ones who would supply us with weapons, who would arm that unit, and I was in favour of that. If things had been different, I guarantee you that I would not have accepted weapons from anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you're saying that the journalist actually tried to pass on his own ideas into your own text.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, this is not my text. I repeat once again. This letter or the report, whatever you call it, I can comment each and every part of it. The ideas that are presented here, the ones that you circled, I would not subscribe to any of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, the idea of a mixed volunteer unit to preserve peace did fall through; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did fall through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know why it fell through?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the name of the journalist who compiled this report?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Said Muminovic. We grew up together in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not going to ask you to speculate. However, let me ask you do you think that peace would have been preserved and prolonged if the idea of the unit had taken off the ground?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, because I was one of the proponents of that idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then the bridge was destroyed and there was an all-out conflict which lasted while you were there; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that a true conflict broke out on the 3rd or the 4th of May. I don't know who the parties to that conflict were because I didn't know who was on the other side. I didn't see who opened fire on the JNA in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And your statement from 2008, according to 92 ter, paragraph 13, says that the war broke out in Brcko on the 3rd of May, 1992. It was a real conflict that lasted throughout the whole period that I spent there, and it takes two to have a conflict. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In that same paragraph, you say that an aircraft flew over and that a tremendous explosion was heard. However, that you had never seen where the alleged missile fell. You didn't see any ruins, et cetera. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were two aircraft, not one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: An explosion was heard, but you didn't see the location where it happened; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once I went in the direction of Mujkici. I saw damaged roofs of buildings and family houses in that particular area. I'm not sure whether that was caused by these aircraft, and I cannot tell you that with any degree of certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that when there is -- a sound barrier is broken that that can also produce a tremendous effect?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that very well, but what I heard were probably bombs dropped by the aircraft.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you're not sure?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sure that they did fire those missiles at certain facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In hindsight, do you now understand the existence of the 108th Brigade, the HVO, and the Birac Motorised Brigade given the conflict broke out on the 3rd of May and lasted throughout the whole time that you were there?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I don't understand your question. Am I supposed to agree with you on the existence of something that I personally did not see?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, we are trying to help the Chamber to realise who was involved in the conflict. You yourself confirmed that the real conflict started there and lasted the whole time. Who was involved in the conflict?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw heavy weaponry belonging to the JNA, that it was firing. However, who was their target and where these guns were pointing at, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that towards the end of April there were groups of troops there wearing a variety of uniforms; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw at the Brcko garrison people dressed in camouflage uniforms and wearing red berets on their heads. As far as I know, such people did not exist before in the Yugoslav People's Army. Those were the people I saw, including the reservists, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that the president of the municipality, the Croat, largely trusted the JNA and was advocating the idea for the JNA to try and preserve peace in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. He appeared on TV and gave statements to this effect. I, myself, also believed in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then you say that when the conflict broke out total chaos ensued and that the situation was confusing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the first victim was a Serb whose last name was Medic who was killed from a mosque near the centre of the town?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time that I hear that from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. 65 ter 22527A, page 150. In the Krajisnik case you said that you did not see any damage caused by the bomb, the aerial bomb; correct?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The aerial bomb, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you went on to say that during and after the fighting in Brcko, the army itself did not commit crimes but that, rather, paramilitary formations were involved in the commission of crimes, and you accused them of the most serious crimes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then you said that during this chaotic situation, paramilitary formations managed to impose their rules in town and to occupy main check-points in the town close to the Tesla factory, Grcica factory, et cetera; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were the ones that I saw in town, but also the ones that you mentioned, all of these points were manned by people who emerged from the JNA barracks in Brcko. They were members of their special units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now look at 22527A, page 90 from the Krajisnik case, please. Page 90, you say -- just a moment. You say from the 12th of May on: [In English] "When I was moving around, I had several opportunities to leave the Elektrodistribucija and go to the town in order to do repairs. In the town, itself, there were several check-points, mixed check-points manned by the people in camouflage uniform for whom I suppose that they belonged to the JNA, and sometimes there would also be one or two police officers wearing regular police uniform. It all depended on check-points." [Interpretation] And you said that Red Berets were there as well in camouflage uniforms and that some of them were local Serbs from Brcko. [In English] "And some of the local Serbs from Brcko, my neighbours, were stopping vehicles and asking for the people's IDs." [Interpretation] Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We don't need to tender this into evidence because I have read this page for the record. You were arrested on the 27th of May and taken to the police station.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is already in the evidence. This is his 92 ter statement.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the police station, you were put in a dark room alongside two other persons; correct?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Those people were already there.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Nobody maltreated you at the statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: One of these two persons was Slavko Bozic. Was he a relative of Rade Bozic who later on released you?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why was this Slavko Bozic arrested?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slavko was a petty criminal before the war. While I was in this room, I chatted with him, and he did not discuss the reason for his being there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So Nedzad Dizdarevic and Slavko Bozic were there and you came there as a third person; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you stated that a man called Jovan Pudic had committed a lot of bad things in Brcko such as the killing of civilians. That was registered by a Reuters correspondent of Serb origin and he sent out photographs all over the world?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we then look at your statement given on the 7th of May, 1993 that's 65 ter 19924, and we need page 3. Page 3 in both English and Serbian. I believe that we need paragraph 9 in Serbian. [In English] "A Serb Reuters correspondent took photos of killings and was later on rewarded for those -- these photos by the World Press Photo jury in Amsterdam." [Interpretation] At the end, he said: [In English] "The policeman shooting men in the photo is Pudic, Jovan." Is this true or not?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, this is a report draft by the Helsinki committee in Denmark. They also showed me the photograph took by Bojan Stojanovic in May of 1992 in Brcko. They asked me if I knew the man who was shooting this other person in the back, and I said that I didn't. In July of 1992, in Belgrade, Mr. Bojan Stojanovic and Rade Bozic brought me a couple of photographs that he also took in May 1992 showing Mr. Pudic, but he was not the one who killed people personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this is not correct that this is Pudic.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, you said that in addition to the killing that we now realise didn't happen, you said that Pudic and his colleagues used to beat you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pudic hit me with a handgun on the back of my neck or on the head when he pushed me into the office. Later on when I was in the hangar, whether it was a colleague of his or not, this one beat me up properly, and I described that in my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, in the case against President Milosevic, you described the situation slightly different. Can we now look at 1D3895. On page 25 of this document you say, starting from line 10: [In English] "Pudic met me and he was a policemen before the war, and I think he's still a policeman actually. So he was there and he wanted to take a pistol to hit me on the head with it, but he changed his mind and took me into an office. Now, why they took me ...," and so on and so on. [Interpretation] Now, it seems that your description was slightly different. He wanted to hit you, but he didn't hit you.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did hit me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, what your said in the Milosevic case is not true.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how this happened, but he did hit me, and he did push me into the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this page admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1567, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, in the Krajisnik case there is also something -- in the Krajisnik case there's also something slightly different, and can we now see 65 ter 225278.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 27A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That is Exhibit P3002.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where did Pudic hit you exactly?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's look at pages 131 and 132. The bottom of the page 131, lines 24, 25: [In English] "That's correct that he didn't hit you?" And you say: "It's correct that he hit me, but in this statement I don't know --" And then 132, please. "... I don't know why it's in the statement the way it is. Well, he did hit me on the side of the head. He did hit me actually on the head, but more on the side to my ear. I don't know why in the statement it says that he did not, but he did hit me on the right side of the head, that is correct."

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So not on the neck but behind your right ear.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, he did hit me with a handgun on my head. Now, I don't know how we're going to describe this, whether it was in -- on the head, on the neck, et cetera. As we say in Bosnia, not directly on the head but actually, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In one statement you say that he took you to the office. In another statement you say that he hit you on the neck, and in the third statement you say that he hit you behind the ear. It's quite different.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You may take it as you wish. What I'm telling you now is how it actually happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, which of the three versions shall we accept and adopt?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't get the answer that the witness gave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your answer was not reflected in the transcript because of the overlap. Could you repeat, Mr. Gasi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The accused asked me, Judge, why I said once that he -- that Pudic hit me on the head. Then I said that he didn't, and the third time I said that he hit me behind my right ear. I was hit with a handgun. Whether it was on the right or the left side, I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, my question was which of the three statements should we choose, and you said, "Whichever you like."

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's consistent with the answer that I gave you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. 1D3891. Can we have a look at that, please. It's a video. It was made by my team, my Defence team, and it's Mr. Pudic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] I'm Jovan Pudic. I was born in 1949 in Grbavica near Brcko. At the beginning of these war events, I had a job in Germany, and I came sometime around the 19th of May. "During the trial in The Hague, I was watching television in my own house, and I saw Gasi, who is also from Brcko, testifying against -- I think it was Krajisnik. At one point in time he mentioned my name, that on the 3rd of May, in front of the place station, he saw me killing people of Bosniak ethnicity. He also testified that he had been detained in Luka and that on the 7th and 10th of May or between the 7th and 10th of May he watched me taking people out with gunshots in the back and that those people no longer returned. "I -- this didn't strike me, because I was not in Brcko during that period at all. I thought it was some kind of mistake. However I'm the only Jovan Pudic. I found it a bit funny. However, people from the Krajisnik Defence came to see me and I gave them a statement. As I showed them documentation that I was employed in Germany until the 15th of May and that I was in possession of documents when I had come out and all of that, I gave them the statement. I can give this same statement to the Karadzic Defence as well."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So he was not a policeman. He was working in Germany, and in the beginning of May when you ascribe these misdeeds to him he was not in Brcko at all?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But, Mr. Karadzic, it seems you and I do not understand each other here. I'm not talking about Jovan Pudic. I'm talking about Branko Pudic, who was a policeman before the war. To this day he's a policeman in Brcko. My apologies to this gentleman. I don't know how his name was brought up here at all. I don't even know this man.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have a look at your statement of the 7th of May, 1993. We did look at it a moment ago. [In English] "The policeman shooting men on the photo is Pudic, Jovan." [Interpretation] That's in your statement, Pudic, Jovan. Can we have a look at it again, 65 ter 19924, and then page 3. 65 ter 19924?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Paragraph number?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 3. Paragraph 9. I have nothing on my screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably we need to switch from Sanction to -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This policeman is Jovan Pudic. That's what you say here, the man in the photograph who was shooting people.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just given you an answer to that. This is an interview given to the Danish Helsinki committee. I never mentioned Jovan Pudic in this document. If I ever mentioned Pudic, it was Branko Pudic who was a policeman in Brcko before the war and who is a policeman to this day in Brcko. I don't know how this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ah-ha. Can we look at page 5, page 5 of this document. It's repeated in the second paragraph on the top of the page. Dragan Zivkovic, Miso Sajevac or Cajevac, Jovan Pudic and Ranko Marinkovic and so on.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Branko Pudic, not Jovan. Branko Pudic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. But it doesn't say Branko here, it says Jovan; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the video be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There's no need to admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then you got to Luka. How long were you at the police station?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, half an hour, 40 minutes, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In various statements of yours you gave testimony describing what happened in the Luka camp. Now I would like us to establish the facts in respect of that camp together with you. My first question will be: Do you remember that the Luka camp was established by the command of the paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have a look at page 4 of this statement that is in e-court now. [No interpretation] [In English] "In the second room there were circa 200 prisoners and Arkan group was in command of the warehouse at Luka." [Interpretation] Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Where did you read that from?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Page 4. We are going to find it. It's the fourth line from the top of the page in English.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The man who beat me up, Mr. Karadzic, is Ivan, a member of Arkan's group.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [In English] "And Arkan's group was in command of the warehouse group." [Interpretation] Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where? Where did you read that from?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In English, it's the fourth line from the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think it may be the previous page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. You're right. Thank you. The last paragraph, number 12 on this page in Serbian. And then it moves on to page 13 -- or, rather, page 23.

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're going back to the report again of the Helsinki committee the one that they wrote up, Mr. Karadzic. I received that report in English perhaps only two months later. As for all of this that was said here, I hadn't signed any of this. I did not sign a single sheet of paper. They didn't give me enough time to make corrections or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So what is written in this statement is not correct; right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would agree with you, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, you mentioned some other men as camp commanders. Did you say that Vojkan Djurkovic was the commander of the camp?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On one occasion Mr. Djurkovic showed up down there in Luka, and he introduced himself as commander of that camp down there at a particular point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He brought you cigarettes and potato chips and other things?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, his men, when he made those speeches.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What were these speeches of his about?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of the prisoners were detained in Luka from the beginning of May, he was actually calling out their names and saying to them that he had personally saved them from being killed, and he said that he tried to protect people as much as he could. Then he called out the names of these people who knew, and he asked them to confirm that before all of us in the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we look at your statement from 1995, 1D3889. Page 10. I believe that it's the same in English. I have the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's the second paragraph in English. You say that everyone knew that Djurkovic was the commander of the camp and that he was the one who could spare your life, that he made speeches, brought people there. And further down it says that when he would leave, the prisoners would get together and say how good Vojkan was; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ISAK GASI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, in your testimony in the trial of President Milosevic, 1D3895, page 4, you said something different. 1D3895. Can this page from the 1995 statement be admitted? Page 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1568, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
